statement: In unconstrained mathematical optimization of a differentiable multivariate function $f$, a descent direction at point $\mathbf{x}$ is a vector direction along which steps are taken to decrease the function value, canonically defined by the opposite direction of the gradient (or approximate gradient): $\mathbf{d} = -\nabla f(\mathbf{x})$, which is the direction of steepest descent (or $-\mathbf{p}_n$ in step updates $\mathbf{a}_n - \eta_n \mathbf{p}_n$).

symbols.meaning: differentiable multivariate objective function to be minimized
search direction vector at iteration n

properties.property: Stepping in the opposite direction of the gradient $-\nabla f(\mathbf{x})$ is the direction of steepest descent.
properties.why: Repeated steps opposite to the gradient decrease a differentiable function toward a local minimum.

properties.property: Stepping in the positive direction of the gradient produces gradient ascent, maximizing the function.
properties.why: The gradient points in the direction of function increase.

properties.property: For quadratic minimization $f(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{x}^\top \mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - 2\mathbf{x}^\top \mathbf{b}$ with symmetric positive-definite $\mathbf{A}$, successive steepest descent directions (residuals $\mathbf{r}_k = \mathbf{b} - \mathbf{A}\mathbf{x}_k$) are mutually orthogonal: $\langle \mathbf{r}_{k+1}, \mathbf{r}_k \rangle = 0$.
properties.why: Line search chooses the locally optimal step size along the current steepest descent direction.

properties.property: In infinite-dimensional function spaces, the descent direction is determined from the Fréchet derivative of the functional.
properties.why: Optimization search spaces can be infinite-dimensional function spaces.

assumptions.assumption: The objective function $f$ is differentiable at the evaluation point.
assumptions.breaks_when: The function is non-differentiable or the gradient cannot be evaluated.

assumptions.assumption: A step size $\eta_n$ can be chosen such that $f(\mathbf{a}_{n} - \eta_n \mathbf{p}_n) \le f(\mathbf{a}_n)$.
assumptions.breaks_when: The step size is chosen too large without line search or curvature bounds, causing the objective function value to increase.

assumptions.assumption: The objective function $f$ is convex (for convergence to a global solution).
assumptions.breaks_when: The function is non-convex, so descent directions can lead to local minima rather than global minima.

failure_modes.signature: Descent directions alternate between extreme axes of elongated level sets with $\langle \mathbf{r}_{k+1}, \mathbf{r}_k \rangle = 0$
failure_modes.cause: High condition number $\kappa(\mathbf{A})$ of the system matrix forces each new direction to undo overshoot from the previous step

failure_modes.mode: Convergence to a non-global local minimum
failure_modes.signature: Gradient norm reaches zero at a point with objective value strictly greater than the global minimum
